name: wordtoolkit
description: Token-lean native Microsoft Word automation with 17 public MCP tools: 13 core actions and 4 capability gateways, exposing 157 native actions lazily.

interface.longDescription: WordToolkit controls installed Microsoft Word through a native .NET bridge and also inspects, validates, compares, repairs, and renders saved DOCX packages without opening Word. The public MCP surface has 17 tools: 13 core actions and 4 capability gateways. Those gateways lazily expose 157 native actions only when needed. Live changes are version-bound, batched, verified, and rollback-aware; saved-package mutations use fingerprint-bound reviewed plans and create-new outputs where required. It supports native editable OfficeMath equations, formatting, tables, fields, comments, tracked review, content controls, SmartArt, references, semantic queries, comparison, reversible patches, merge, Open XML SDK validation, and Word-authoritative PDF/PNG export. Compact responses avoid echoed payloads, while full contracts and diagnostics remain available on demand. Optional local providers cover LibreOffice rendering, Tesseract OCR, and complete-document TeX compilation with explicit capability limits. It blocks unsafe raw COM/XML paths, macros, DDE, silent overwrites, stale tokens, ambiguous targets, and unverified recovery. Structural validation does not pretend to prove layout quality, so document work that depends on appearance still ends with rendered-page inspection.
capabilities: Semantic query, compare, patch, and merge
Word PDF and PNG export with visual QA
Comments, review, fields, tables, and structures
Lazy action schemas and compact responses
Local .NET runtime with no Python dependency
Optional local OCR, LibreOffice, and TeX providers
defaultPrompt: Create a polished Word document in one verified batch and export it to PDF.
Open my Word document, make the requested edits, validate it, and save a new copy.
Inspect this DOCX, explain concrete problems, and apply only the repairs I approve.
